$comment: The source of sf-avatars's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/avatars (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

fields.summary: JSON text of the fields the attributes below also take (imageUrl, avatarUrl, avatarSize, active, check, name, source, labelText, labelSecondText, avatars, avatarsMore); an attribute wins over its field

property.summary: JSON text of the sizes the attributes round-size, label-size and profile-size also take

avatars.summary: The group's avatars: an image, else its text (initials); the attribute takes the list as JSON text too

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

user.$comment: The user combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="user".

group.$comment: The group combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="group".

label.$comment: The label combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="label".

profile.$comment: The profile combination of the one Lit template in JavaScript (§5.2 migration form), chosen by template="profile".

accessibility.$comment: Pictures beside visible text: each avatar is a span whose image has alt="" and is hidden from assistive technology; the visible text (name, label, the remainder) names the person or the group. Nothing takes focus.
accessibility.name: none

x-summary: Ready combinations of avatars: a person with a source, a stacked group with a remainder, an avatar with two lines of label, and a profile avatar with a verified badge. Drawn from sf-avatar's parts; for a single avatar with a name or a card use sf-avatar.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-avatars when the interface needs the avatars behavior.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

x-renamed: settings.data → fields: "data" is a reserved name (§3.1); data is its dated alias
x-decisions: a11y-role: none; a11y-name: none (the old shape "internal" meant the same). The avatars are pictures beside visible text -- the image alt="" and aria-hidden, the name, label or remainder printed -- and nothing takes focus; for an avatar that is a control use sf-avatar.

data -> fields: data is a reserved name (§3.1), so the JSON text of the fields is fields and data its dated setting alias (aliases.json, until 2026-12-01). It stays a string of JSON text, as the attribute always was; an attribute of the same field wins over it.

item-shape: avatars is a list whose entries are {image-url, text} (§4.2); image_url and initials are still read. The attribute takes the list as JSON text, as before; the property takes the list itself.
active is a value (out): the online dot the default template shows; it keeps its default, so a page that wrote active still writes the attribute.

templates: default, user, group, label and profile are the combinations of one Lit template in JavaScript (js/templates/default.js), the migration form §5.2 allows; the old template/*/index.html files are not compiled and stay as they were.
docs: the folder had no docs.md; it gains one (§3).

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (the label combination: Команда проекта, 5 участников) plus a person with a source, a group with a remainder, a profile and the default with the online dot.

css-variables: the five --sf-avatar-* public variables of the class sheet sf-avatars draws with (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json, avatar), as sf-code-input declares the verification sheet's (§6).
version 1.1.0: a renamed member behind a dated alias is a minor (§4.10, §16.20).
